title: Evidence coverage measurement (foundational)
description: Signature original: Coverage is measured as the fraction of the mission's subquestions that have at least one supporting source above the support threshold. A mission can feel complete while half its subquestions are actually unanswered; the coverage number makes the gap visible. Coverage is recomputed after every batch of new evidence. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
subs = {'q1': 0.8, 'q2': 0.5, 'q3': 0.1, 'q4': 0.7}
TH = 0.35
cov = sum(1 for s in subs.values() if s >= TH) / len(subs)
print(f'evidence coverage: {cov:.0%}')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Stopping-Criterion Evaluator, 2026-10-21.

title: Sufficiency threshold per mission type (foundational)
description: Signature original: The sufficiency threshold is set from the mission's stakes: a casual overview stops at 60 percent coverage, a decision-grade investigation demands 90. Thresholds are declared in the mission plan, not improvised mid-search when fatigue sets in. Declared thresholds keep stopping honest. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
thresholds = {'overview': 0.6, 'decision-grade': 0.9}
mission, coverage = 'decision-grade', 0.75
print('sufficient:', coverage >= thresholds[mission], f'({coverage:.0%} vs {thresholds[mission]:.0%} needed)')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Stopping-Criterion Evaluator, 2026-10-21.

title: Marginal value estimate of continuing (foundational)
description: Signature original: Before deciding, the evaluator estimates the marginal value of more searching: the recent rate of new-evidence discovery times the importance of the still-unanswered subquestions. If the discovery rate has flatlined, continuing is unlikely to help no matter how important the gaps are. The estimate turns 'should we keep going' from a feeling into a number. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
recent_new = [5, 3, 1, 0]  # new evidence per batch
gap_importance = 0.8
marginal = (sum(recent_new[-2:]) / 2) * gap_importance
print('marginal value of continuing:', round(marginal, 2), '-> STOP' if marginal < 1 else '-> CONTINUE')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Stopping-Criterion Evaluator, 2026-10-21.

title: Stop/continue decision record (foundational)
description: Signature original: The decision is recorded with its inputs: coverage, threshold, marginal value, and the resulting verdict. A recorded decision can be audited later, which matters when someone asks why an investigation stopped with questions open. The record also notes who or what made the call. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).

title: Continue plan with targeted gaps (foundational)
description: Signature original: When the verdict is continue, the evaluator outputs a targeted plan naming exactly which subquestions remain and what kind of evidence would close each. Targeted continuation beats undirected 'search more' every time. The plan becomes the next iteration's marching orders for the search agent. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
gaps = ['q3: needs a primary source on cache TTL behavior']
print('continue plan:')
for g in gaps: print(' -', g)
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Stopping-Criterion Evaluator, 2026-10-21.
